A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KL-Shampoo/KL-SOAP research. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v8 reports original language-model pretraining experiments, with optimizer test-loss comparisons in Section 6 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v9 retains these original experiments and results, including the larger Llama3-450M comparison in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The KL-Shampoo/KL-SOAP objectives, updates, QR/EMA components, and practical algorithm in Figure 12 are unchanged. The corrected explanatory identity does not alter an algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same language-model pretraining tasks on FineWeb, C4, and OpenWebText subsets, including the Llama3-450M/FineWeb3.3B experiment in Appendix H.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the experiments. Muon already appears alongside KL-Shampoo and SOAP in v8 Figure 9; its new discussion and citation do not add an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain the same model configurations, token and batch budgets, learning-rate schedules, tuning procedures, and decomposition frequency and precision settings.

E4.justification: The grafting ablation in Figure 2, instantaneous-versus-EMA eigenvalue test in Figure 4, and F-/VN-Shampoo variant analyses in Figures 7 and 10 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Run-count disclosures and statistical-reporting practices are unchanged. No seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: The result curves, numerical entries, and reported rankings are unchanged throughout both PDFs, including Figure 9's per-iteration versus wall-clock comparison with Muon.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects E[GG^T] = S_a^*/Tr(S_b^*) to E[GG^T] = Tr(S_b^*) S_a^*. This repairs the matrix-Gaussian moment identity and makes it consistent with the retained update in Equation (14). The appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the KL framework, optimizer performance, SOAP-level per-iteration runtime, and avoidance of Adam-related memory overhead in KL-Shampoo.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly characterizes the existing whitening interpretation as two-sided statistical gradient orthogonalization and distinguishes it from short- or one-sided deterministic, SVD-based orthogonalization such as Muon. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Code access and implementation information are retained, including Figure 12's momentum, weight decay, damping/clipping, eigenvalue initialization, and low-precision storage details.

R1.justification: v9 adds Jordan's Muon reference (2024a) and a brief conceptual comparison in Section 3.2. This modestly extends positioning relative to gradient orthogonalization methods.

P1.justification: v9 adds one explanatory sentence in Section 3.2 and updates citation labels and the version/date stamp. The narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 shifts downward on page 6, and surrounding prose and bibliography entries reflow. Section 5's heading moves from page 8 to page 9. Figure and table contents and designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v9 corrects an inconsistent matrix-moment identity in Section 3.3, aligning the explanation with Equation (14), and clarifies the distinction from Muon in Section 3.2. These provide limited gains in mathematical accuracy and exposition; the methods, empirical evidence, and appendices are unchanged.
